citation: Prat, F., Castro, M., Llorens, D., Marzal, A., & Vilar, J. (2008). UJI Pen Characters (Version 2) [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5FG8S.
source_format: Version 2 WORD / NUMSTROKES / POINTS n # x y ...; sample file UTF-8; uji2.names Latin-1.

selection_plan.choice_basis: Selected for this study before examining measurements or correlation results; one common character, same label for all writers and repetitions.
selection_plan.calibration: Divide raw max-minus-min ink-coordinate extents by the site ratio documented by dataset authors: UJI=100 ink units/mm, UPV=152 ink units/mm.
selection_plan.dependence_analysis_unit: The 60 writer-level paired means, averaging both repetitions separately for width and height
selection_plan.inclusion_rule: All source samples with exact character label a; both repetitions of all 60 writers
selection_plan.exclusion_rule: Other character labels only; no selected glyphs dropped or selected using their measured values
selection_plan.planned_site_sensitivity: Report association separately for UJI and UPV as well as pooled calibrated writer means

derived_quantities.width_ink: max(X)-min(X), over all points of all strokes; no +1
derived_quantities.height_ink: max(Y)-min(Y), over all points of all strokes; no +1
derived_quantities.physical_interpretation: Screen-coordinate millimetres using site calibration in uji2.names; not measurements on paper.

preprocessing.unselected_characters: 11520 glyphs excluded solely because character != a, as prespecified.

dependence_analysis_unit: 60 paired writer means in screen millimetres; each writer contributes one pair based on both repetitions.
site_caveat: UJI and UPV use different coordinate scales (100 and 152 ink units/mm). Pooling unconverted ink extents would introduce a site scale confound. Screen-mm conversion corrects this documented scale, but site and population differences remain for sensitivity analysis.
limitations: Characters were written in guided acquisition boxes on a tablet, not free writing on paper.
The 60 writers are not documented as a random sample of a general population.
Two repeated sessions per writer are not treated as independent writers.
Only XY coordinates were recorded: no time or pressure information exists.
